questions.question: What is the largest animal alive today?
questions.explanation: The blue whale can exceed 25 metres in length and weigh well over 100 tonnes.

questions.question: Which part of a cell is known as its 'powerhouse'?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce most of the cell's usable energy, in the form of ATP.

questions.question: Which gas do plants absorb from the air for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugars, releasing oxygen.

questions.question: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explanation: An octopus has three hearts: two pump blood to the gills and one to the rest of the body.

questions.question: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.explanation: Cheetahs can reach about 100 km/h in short sprints.

questions.question: What do giant pandas mainly eat?
questions.explanation: Bamboo makes up about 99% of a giant panda's diet.

questions.question: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: The skin covers roughly 1.5 to 2 square metres in an adult.

questions.question: How many bones are in an adult human body?
questions.explanation: Adults have 206 bones; babies are born with more, which later fuse.

questions.question: Which blood cells carry oxygen around the body?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds oxygen in the lungs.

questions.question: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The stapes, in the middle ear, is about 3 mm long.

questions.question: What is the process by which a caterpillar becomes a butterfly called?
questions.explanation: Metamorphosis is a complete change of body form between life stages.

questions.question: Which of these animals is a marsupial?
questions.explanation: Marsupials, like kangaroos, carry their young in a pouch after a very short pregnancy.

questions.question: What is a group of lions called?
questions.explanation: A group of lions is a pride.

questions.question: Acorns are the seeds of which tree?
questions.explanation: Oak trees produce acorns.

questions.question: Bees collect which substance from flowers to make honey?
questions.explanation: Bees collect nectar and convert it to honey by evaporation and enzymes.

questions.question: Which is the only mammal capable of true, sustained flight?
questions.explanation: Bats can fly with their wings. Flying squirrels and gliders only glide.

questions.question: Which is the tallest tree species in the world?
questions.explanation: Coast redwoods can exceed 115 metres in height.

questions.question: What is the scientific study of birds called?
questions.explanation: Ornithology is the study of birds. Entomology is insects and herpetology is reptiles and amphibians.

questions.question: Which part of the eye adjusts the size of the pupil?
questions.explanation: Muscles in the iris widen or narrow the pupil to control how much light enters the eye.

questions.question: Which is the largest living species of cat?
questions.explanation: The tiger is the largest cat, with Siberian tigers reaching around 300 kg.

questions.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: The heart has two atria and two ventricles.

questions.question: Which vitamin does the skin produce when exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: UVB light triggers vitamin D synthesis in the skin.

questions.question: True or false: botanically, a banana is a berry.
questions.explanation: Botanically, a berry develops from a single ovary and has soft flesh and seeds. Bananas qualify, while strawberries do not.

questions.question: True or false: goldfish only have a three-second memory.
questions.explanation: Studies show goldfish can remember things for weeks or months and can be trained.

questions.question: True or false: humans only use 10% of their brains.
questions.explanation: Brain imaging shows activity across virtually the whole brain; the 10% claim is a myth.

questions.question: Which living bird has the largest wingspan?
questions.explanation: The wandering albatross has a wingspan of up to about 3.5 metres.

questions.question: How many legs does an adult insect have?
questions.explanation: All insects have six legs. Spiders have eight and are not insects.

questions.question: Which plant tissue carries water upward from the roots to the leaves?
questions.explanation: Xylem carries water and minerals up; phloem carries sugars around the plant.

questions.question: Which amphibian is famous for its ability to regrow lost limbs?
questions.explanation: Axolotls can regenerate limbs, parts of the heart and even parts of the brain.

questions.question: Which mammal lays eggs?
questions.explanation: The platypus and echidnas are monotremes, the only mammals that lay eggs.
